title: Late changes to erection sequences can leave beams vulnerable to lateral-torsional buckling
excerpt: CROSS-UK Report 1479 (13 January 2026) describes a near-miss on a filler beam bridge deck. A late contractor change from lifting beams in connected pairs to lifting them individually introduced a critical temporary stability risk of lateral-torsional buckling under wet concrete. Utilisation exceeded 200% without bracing. The case underlines the need for early communication of temporary conditions, independent checking of sequence changes, and active Temporary Works Coordinator oversight so that temporary states are not assumed to be less critical than the permanent condition.
linkedinReady:
Late changes to the intended construction sequence can introduce critical temporary stability risks that are not present in the final permanent condition.

CROSS-UK Report 1479 (published 13 January 2026) describes a near-miss on an approximately 20 m span filler beam bridge deck. Shortly before the Category II check was completed, the contractor altered the sequence from lifting steel beams in connected pairs (with precast concrete infill providing temporary stability) to lifting them individually. This created a significant risk of lateral-torsional buckling of the unbraced beams under the weight of wet concrete during construction. Assessment showed utilisation factors over 200% without rotational restraint at the flange ends or suitable bracing. Temporary LTB restraints were therefore necessary.

Even after the issue was identified, the contractor and temporary works designer later challenged the necessity of the bracing again, close to the concrete pour. By that stage reinforcement was largely fixed, restricting space for installation. The event was classified as a near-miss. It illustrates how late changes, unclear design responsibility for temporary conditions, and incomplete understanding of temporary stability modes can compress design and checking time and raise the risk of error.

HSE guidance on structural stability during alteration, demolition and dismantling is clear: temporary supports must be designed, installed and maintained to withstand foreseeable loads. Structures should never be overloaded. Temporary bracing or propping may be required where permanent elements that provide restraint are not yet in place or where the load path changes. Any temporary structure must be used only for the purposes for which it was designed. BS 5975-1:2024 provides the industry framework for managing temporary works, including the role of the Temporary Works Coordinator in ensuring clarity of responsibility and control of changes.

Provisional category only — to be confirmed by the TWC and the project temporary works procedure. Do not proceed until reviewed and accepted under the project temporary works procedure.

Educational only. Not for construction.

body.p: CROSS-UK Report 1479, published on 13 January 2026, concerns a filler beam bridge deck of approximately 20 m span. During the final stages of design and shortly before the Category II check was completed, the contractor changed the intended construction sequence. Instead of lifting steel beams in connected pairs (with the concrete infill precast to provide temporary stability for each pair), the beams were to be lifted individually. The change introduced a significant temporary stability concern: the risk of lateral-torsional buckling of the beams under the weight of the wet concrete applied during construction. The Category II checker identified that the main beams, if left unbraced and without rotational restraint at the ends of the flanges, could experience buckling under a utilisation factor of over 200%. Temporary LTB restraints were required. The designer confirmed this and notified the contractor. Later, approximately three months after the initial resolution and just two weeks before the deck concrete was scheduled to be cast, the contractor and their temporary works designer challenged the necessity of the temporary bracing again. Discussions involved commercial and programme considerations around design responsibility. Eventually the permanent works designer prepared a bracing scheme that tied the inner girders back to the precast edge beams, but by that stage most of the deck reinforcement had been fixed, restricting available space. The design and check programme was compressed. The reporter classified the event as a near-miss.

Temporary works provide an engineered solution to support or protect a structure during construction or to ensure stability while permanent elements are not yet providing their final restraint. CDM 2015 places duties on the principal contractor to plan, manage and monitor the construction phase, and on contractors to plan, manage and monitor their own work. HSE guidance on structural stability during alteration, demolition and dismantling states that temporary support must be designed, installed and maintained to withstand foreseeable loads and that structures should never be overloaded. Temporary bracing and propping may be required where the structure is subjected to changed load paths, where permanent bracing is not yet in place, or where the footprint or restraint changes during the work. HSE temporary works guidance further requires that any temporary structure is designed, installed and maintained to withstand any foreseeable loads and is only used for the purposes for which it was designed. BS 5975-1:2024 sets out management procedures for the control of temporary works as recognised industry good practice (it is not a statute). Late changes to erection or construction sequences can alter the temporary stability condition in ways that are not covered by the permanent works design assumptions. Independent checking and clear communication between permanent works designers, temporary works designers and the Temporary Works Coordinator are essential to identify such risks before they reach site. Provisional category only — to be confirmed by the TWC and the project temporary works procedure.

body.h: Practical TWC and TWS control points
ul: Ensure the design brief for temporary works explicitly addresses temporary stability at every stage of the construction sequence, including lifting, temporary placement, and before permanent restraint or bracing is effective.

Require that any proposed change to the construction sequence or method is referred to the Temporary Works Coordinator and the relevant designers before it is adopted. Changes that affect temporary stability must be subject to design and independent check.
Confirm that temporary bracing or restraint for lateral-torsional buckling (or other modes) has been designed for the actual temporary configuration, not assumed from the permanent condition.
Verify that responsibility for temporary condition design is clear between permanent works designer, temporary works designer and contractor, and that the TWC has oversight.
Where reinforcement or other permanent works have progressed, assess whether late introduction of bracing remains practical; if not, stop and review the sequence.
At permit-to-load or equivalent, confirm that installed temporary restraints match the checked design and that no unapproved changes have been made.
Treat late challenges to the necessity of temporary works as a trigger for formal review rather than informal agreement.
Do not proceed until the temporary stability arrangement, including any sequence changes, has been reviewed and accepted by the competent person under the project temporary works procedure.

body.p: Educational briefing only. Not for construction. Based on CROSS-UK Report 1479 and HSE guidance on temporary works and structural stability. It is not a design, a check or a statement that any particular temporary works arrangement is adequate or inadequate. No utilisation factors, bracing sizes or capacities have been calculated here. Subject to project-specific verification and acceptance under the project temporary works procedure. AI-assisted drafting requires competent review before use on site.
